consensus_summary: Mainstream Christian reading takes “shadow of death” as extreme death-associated darkness—mortal peril, deep gloom, the approach of death, or spiritual hopelessness—through which God accompanies his people and which Christ’s light dispels (esp. Ps 23:4; Isa 9:2 // Matt 4:16; Luke 1:79), with a live philological alternative of plain “deep darkness.”
book_summary: The book defines a shadow as the outline/boundary of its subject, so the Shadow of Death is the boundary of Death’s mountain-kingdom; the Ps 23 valley is the low passage between mountain-kingdoms by which the Shepherd leads people from Death’s darkness into Christ’s kingdom of light—the inverse of the Shadow of Christ.
consensus_core_identification: Deathly extreme darkness/peril (or spiritual darkness) experienced or traversed under God’s presence or dispelled by messianic light.
book_core_identification: The boundary-mark of Death’s mountain-kingdom; the valley-border passage from Death’s kingdom into Christ’s.
boundary_disagreement: Consensus admits overlapping cases (mortal danger, dying, Sheol/gloom, spiritual darkness, despair, sometimes mere deep darkness). The book reclassifies the referent as a kingdom-boundary in a mountain-kingdom map, centers the Ps 23 valley as inter-kingdom passage into Christ’s realm, pairs it as inverse of the Shadow of Christ, and does not treat free-floating gloom, depression, or non-kingdom darkness as the core sense.
material_contradiction: None at the center: the book does not deny death-darkness or the God-led passage; it embeds those associations in a stricter symbolic geography the consensus does not use.
rationale: Minimum cores still share the same biblical cluster (Ps 23 valley; darkness-to-light / deliverance into another dominion) rather than replacing the referent with an unrelated object. The book preserves that general death-darkness/passage category but materially tightens identity, conditions, and extension via shadow-as-boundary and Death-vs-Christ mountain-kingdoms—hence REFINED (narrowing/reclassification), not MATCH, not a full core contradiction (DIVERGENT), and not absence from the consensus’s covered texts/senses (NOVEL).
strongest_objection: Standard lexical and pastoral consensus reads tsalmaveth as deathly gloom or deep darkness itself, not as the geometric boundary of a “Death mountain-kingdom”; that ontology and the Shadow-of-Christ inverse depend on the book’s cross-chapter system (mountain/shadow) more than on the printed verses alone.
